items: Giant stars live much longer than dwarf stars.
Compared to dwarf stars, giant stars have a greater rate of nuclear reactions.
prompt: Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?

options.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
options.b: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
options.c: Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
options.d: Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct

ex.summary: A star's mass decides how fast it burns. Massive stars need very high rates of nuclear fusion in their cores to hold themselves up against their own gravity, so they use up their hydrogen in a few million years, while small dwarf stars burn slowly and can shine for billions or even trillions of years. So the fusion-rate statement is true, and the longer-life statement is the reverse of the truth.

aarav.line: Bigger star, more fuel, longer life. Both true.

priya.line: Wait. Faster burning means a shorter life.

verdicts.p: Massive stars last only a few million years; red dwarfs, up to trillions.
More mass, more gravity: they must fuse hydrogen far faster.

source: UPSC key 2024; NASA Science: Star Basics

points.p: about 10 billion years on the main sequence.

extra.source: NASA Science; NASA Imagine the Universe; Nobel Prize 2017

trap: Aarav thought more fuel means a longer life. Giants burn it so fast they die first.
method: Judge each statement alone first; then ask if II explains I or disproves it.

bonus.short: Scientists observed giant black holes merging billions of light-years away. Why did it matter?

reply_right: Bigger stars' gravity drives far faster fusion, so they die sooner.
reply_trap: More fuel isn't longer life: giants burn it so fast they die first.
